verdict.rationale: RudderStack Profiles documents warehouse-native identity resolution. Users declare entities in version-controlled YAML, which generates SQL that handles identity resolution, and builds identity graphs from any combination of unique identifiers across sources, so the rules are documented and configurable. However, the evidence never explicitly describes stitching anonymous activity to known users or linking across devices, and the depth of rule configuration is shown only at summary level. Missing for 10: explicit anonymous-to-known stitching documentation, cross-device merge evidence, detailed identity-rule configuration docs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, anonymous and known activity stitches into one customer profile across devices, with documented and configurable identity-resolution rules

citations.quote: Resolve identities and build a customer 360 in your warehouse.

you declare entities and their attributes in version-controlled YAML, and the system generates warehouse-native SQL that handles identity resolution, incremental computation, and feature aggregation automatically.
Seamlessly generate identity graphs from any combination of unique identifiers across any number data sources.
